name: Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawTexturedPass
signature: void Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawTexturedPass(Gfx_ModelInstance* self, unsigned* cmdList, unsigned arg3, int* state, int* mode)

name: Ui_StatusWindow_Build
signature: void Ui_StatusWindow_Build(UiStatusWindow* self, u32 characterId, const CharacterRecord* record, u32 arg4)
summary: Builds the character status window from a CharacterRecord: lays out the stat rows, model placeholders, animation controllers and transforms of the status screen.

name: maybe_Battle_ActorAction_UpdateHitSequence
summary: Per-frame state machine of a battle actor action (states 0x1324..0x1386): clears the actor's hit flag, spawns message/damage popups at the Spine03 node, sets effect-part directions, plays the associated SEs and advances the linked effects.

The old 'UpdatePose' was wrong - no pose or blend values are written - but the sequence itself is not named anywhere, so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpritePass
signature: void Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpritePass(int self, int cmdList, unsigned arg3, unsigned arg4, int arg5, unsigned char arg6, unsigned arg7, int arg8, unsigned arg9, int arg10)

name: Battle_MonsterPanel_Build
signature: void Battle_MonsterPanel_Build(int rowTableId, BattleRowCtx* ctx, int def)
summary: Builds a monster battle-row panel: resolves the monster record, measures the name, computes the HP-bar origin/fill/span and writes the numeric label segments plus the blink animation.
evidence: Battle_Message_BuildRowForMonsterEx (0x00496C54) dispatches to it in the monster-row branch (local_35c == 1) after Ui_LayoutParams_Init, and the body calls the named Battle_Monster_CalcHpBarFill/CalcHpBarOrigin/CalcBarPercent/CalcBarSpan plus Text_UpdateRowBlink in exactly that order.

name: Battle_Row_SumHpBar
summary: Builds the summed-HP battle row for a party group: adds the HP-derived values of up to four matched actor slots, converts the total into a bar fill, applies the hit flash and writes the three label segments.
evidence: The same named caller Battle_Message_BuildRowForMonsterEx dispatches to it in the other row branch (local_35c == 0) as the alternative to Battle_MonsterPanel_Build, and the body sums the row's actor slots before calling the named Battle_Monster_CalcHpBarFill/CalcHpBarOrigin; 'Sum' therefore describes the summed party HP bar, not turn priority.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawReflectionPass
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawReflectionPass(int self, int cmdList, unsigned arg3, unsigned arg4, unsigned arg5)
summary: Special model-instance pass that builds a 0x100-byte texture matrix and emits the instance parts with it; only used by the overlay main-screen renderer when the Field2D/overlay state f_1310 is set.
evidence: Callers are now named: Gfx_Overlay_DrawMainScreen (0x002D36C8) and its B variant call it after Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawAllPasses / Gfx_Overlay_DrawSprite, gated on manager->f_1310 and passing f_bc/f_c0. That fixes a special screen pass, but nothing in the command block proves the 'reflection' (mirrored) interpretation, so the name stays maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawAlphaBlendPass
signature: void Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawAlphaBlendPass(int self, int cmdList, unsigned arg3, int* state, int* mode)
summary: Alpha-blend draw pass: computes the blend factors (including the gamma path through std_Powf) and installs the alpha state before emitting each part.
evidence: The named dispatcher 0x0056AFFC calls it exactly when the material's alpha triple f_11c/f_120/f_124 is not all 1.0, and Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawAllPasses has the identical guard before the call; that condition plus the blend-state writes makes the alpha-blend reading solid.

name: maybe_Party_GetMessageTokenParams
summary: Scans the living party members (HP, equipment and skill/state flags) and writes a 6-byte result {u32 value, u16 state} whose first byte is 0xFF when no member qualifies and 1..3 for the qualifying case; the callers pass it straight to Ui_Window_BuildMessageArgFromToken to build a battle UI message argument.
evidence: The named callers show the real contract: Ui_Window_GetMessageArg (0x002A2C1C), Ui_SakusenWindow_PushCommandForCursor (0x002A16E8) and maybe_Ui_Window_BuildMessageArgFromToken pass a 6-byte stack buffer and then use it as the token parameters. The old 'FieldModel_UpdateAll(FieldScene*)' was wrong - that argument is a token out-param and the body never touches field models - but the qualifying rule is still not identified, so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateStateMachine
summary: Battle UI per-frame update: advances the unit-list/animation state, drains pending battle-log entries and spawns the queued multi-actor popups for the current battle state.
evidence: The body calls the named Battle_PrepareUnitListUi, Battle_Ui_AllUnitsReady, Battle_Ui_UpdateUnitAnimState, Battle_Ui_FlushPendingLogEntries and Battle_UpdateUnitTransform, so a battle-UI update is certain; this is a recovered entry point without a readable caller and the state numbering is lost, so the state-machine wording stays maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Battle_Effect_UpdateLinkSegment
summary: Updates one effect link segment: copies the eleven-word link description from src into self+0x20, builds its transform, normalises the direction vector and updates or creates the linked effect instance.
evidence: Ten named callers now use it as the shared link-segment step (Battle_ActorAction_UpdateComposite/UpdateMotion, Battle_Effect_UpdateLinkSegments, Effect_SpawnAttachedPair, Field_Gimmick_UpdateEffectLink and the ActorAction effect spawners), always right after Gfx_ModelAttach_SetLocatorPair* and before Battle_Effect_UpdateAuraEffect; the body resolves the instance through the named Effect_FindOrCreateInstance.

name: maybe_Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonA
signature: void maybe_Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonA(FieldNpc* self, const NpcPlacement* p, const u32* color, u32 owner)
summary: NPC placement-record initialiser with an explicit colour: copies the transform from p[8..13], stores *color into the balloon colour field f_38c, forces the balloon flag f_35d = 1, builds the sprite/model children and registers the actor sprite.
evidence: The body is confirmed again as the explicit-colour NPC placement initialiser (transform copy, self->f_38c = *color, f_35d = 1, Field_Actor_CreateSprite + Model_SetupObject); no caller or vtable slot names the NPC balloon object, so the 'Balloon' word remains an inference and the name stays maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonB
signature: void maybe_Field_Npc_InitColorBalloonB(FieldNpc* self, const NpcPlacement* p, const u32* color, u32 owner)
summary: Variant of the explicit-colour NPC placement initialiser: same transform/model/sprite sequence as 0x002FA83C but with a different record offset base and colour mode, used where the caller already resolved the colour.
evidence: Re-read as the same body family as 0x002FA83C (transform copy, colour word, f_35d, Field_Actor_CreateSprite/Model_SetupObject) with a different record base; it still has no caller or vtable sibling that says which NPC kind selects it, so both the 'B' ordinal and 'Balloon' remain inferences and it stays maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_UpdateCameraRelativeSprite
summary: Keeps a camera-facing sprite attached to its owner: advances along the distance curve with Math_Curve_GetPosition/GetTangent, rebuilds the billboard basis, draws the sprite variant and moves the owner's draw offset; releases the effect when the curve is exhausted.
evidence: The named callees Math_Curve_GetPosition/GetTangent, Gfx_Scene_SpriteCtx_Init and Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection confirm a curve-driven billboard sprite update; the only caller (0x0041F6D0) is still unnamed, so the 'camera-relative' part stays inferred and the name stays maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawShadowPass
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawShadowPass(Gfx_ModelInstance* self, int cmdList, unsigned arg3, int* state, int* mode)
summary: Projected model-instance pass: builds the projection matrices through 0x00673BC8/0x00672E44, stamps the command block and emits each part.
evidence: The named dispatcher calls it when material f_254 == 1 and f_cc > 0, between the multi-state and textured passes, and the body feeds the named Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteUniformFloats / Gfx_ModelInstance_BindTextureAndDraw. The matrix build fits a projected pass, but neither f_254 nor the call site proves 'shadow', so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Gfx_ComputeActorScreenPosition
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ComputeActorScreenPosition(float* out, void* arg2, void* record, void* camera, void* arg5)
summary: Computes a camera-relative placement point for an actor: takes the camera record's rotation/position (f_8C..f_A4), the model height for the actor id from the data manager and the bytes at arg2+0x32/+0x33, then writes a 3-float point clamped by Camera_FindEntryCoveringPosition.
evidence: Three named field-NPC callers use the result as a point: Field_NpcJumpAction_PlanPath stores it into action+0x48, Field_Npc_UpdateMoveTarget and Field_NpcGetActionAnimId feed the visible-target list. 'Screen' is not literally proven (no projection matrix is built), but the rotation/height/ray-probe body matches an actor placement point, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Battle_CutsceneObject_Init
signature: void Battle_CutsceneObject_Init(BattleCutscene* self, u32 id, u32 flags, int* params)
summary: Initialises a battle cutscene object: reserves its resource handles from the '.btcs' name, registers the paired TCS scene data and sets up the animation and intrusive-list state.
evidence: The callers now name the object: Battle_CutsceneAnimObject_Dtor (0x005B09F8) and maybe_Battle_CutsceneObject_InitFromParams (0x003615A8) both use it, and the '.btcs' literal plus the named Gfx_ModelInstance_InitWithTransform / Model_Node_ComputeWorldMatrix / Anim_KeyframeTrack_EvaluateAll callees fix the cut-scene-object reading; only the partially lost control flow in the 2396-byte body keeps it below 0.6. The decompiler also flags this body as damaged (unaff_ registers), but that damage is confined to register allocation in the animation setup; the '.btcs' literal, the vtable store and the named callers that decide the name are intact.

name: maybe_Field_Object_UpdateStandPosition
summary: Picks a stand point/rotation for a field object: with a rail table at self+0x314 it copies the current rail point's position and rotation; otherwise it probes up to ten random offsets around the target node at self+0x318, keeps the first collision-free spot and writes it to +0x328..+0x33C.
evidence: The named callers all pass field objects, not cameras: Field_Object_ApplySpawnRecord (0x001846EC) calls it right after applying a spawn record and before Field_Actor_CreateSprite, Model_SetupObject calls it after resolving the model, and Actor_UpdateApproachMove calls it when an interaction starts. The old 'Camera_UpdateFollowPosition' named the wrong owner; the trigger/name of the chosen point is still not certain, so maybe_ at 0.42.

name: Monster_FormatEffectText
signature: void Monster_FormatEffectText(u32 effectId, int kind, int member, MonsterWork* work, u32 arg5, u8 arg6, u8 arg7)
summary: Builds the eight battle message layout rows for an effect cast: copies the default layout table for the effect id, fills the parameter block from the caster/monster record and appends the rows through 0x00326428; kind selects the cast/effect/resist variant.
evidence: Five named battle-row builders call it (Battle_CalcDefenseReduction, Battle_MessageRow_BuildLayout, Battle_Monster_GetEffectValue, maybe_Battle_ApplyMonsterEffect, maybe_Battle_Monster_UpdateConditionRow) with an effect id and kind 0..3 and then mark the text layout dirty; the body resolves the id through the named SpellRecord lookup 0x0063CFC8 and emits 8 rows, so the effect-text reading is supported.

name: maybe_Battle_CalcMemberStatScale
summary: Returns a float resistance/status multiplier for a party member and stat index: reads the member's float tables at +0x998 and +0xD58 (the +0xB68/+0xD74/+0xF28/+0x1134 blocks for index 7), applies the status-0x4F check and Battle_CalcRandomDamageVariance, then combines the factors.
evidence: Re-read the body: the first argument is a stat index (compared with 7 and used with *4 strides) and the second is the PartyMember resolved through func_0035EB98, so the old 'turn priority' reading and its argument names were wrong. The named callers are damage-row builders (Battle_RollMultiHitDamage, Battle_Message_BuildConditionRow) that multiply the returned factor into a displayed value; the exact stat tables at +0x998/+0xD58 are unidentified, so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Field_Object_UpdateVisibilityByRay
summary: Ray-tests the object's stored point (position, -direction, 100.0) through the scene ray helper; when the ray is clear it deactivates the object's children, otherwise it releases the model nodes - a visibility/occlusion update, not a camera move.
evidence: The body never writes a new position back to self, so the old Event_Camera_MoveToPoint was a placeholder; its named callees Field_Collision_RaycastScene, Field_Object_DeactivateChildren, Gfx_ReleaseModelNodes and Field_SceneNode_GetPosition match a ray-based show/hide pass. No caller names the trigger, so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Field_SceneObject_CreateVariantEffects
summary: Applies the object's variant/effect ids (f_B2, f_B3, the u16 at +0x2CA) by creating the corresponding item model or effect model, spawning the scaled effect for id 0x2B and forwarding to the attached object's effect spawner.
evidence: The named caller GimmickItemEffectStart (0x0015D158) reaches it after resolving a gimmick item record, and the body dispatches on f_B2/f_B3/+0x2CA to the named Field_SceneObject_CreateItemModel, Field_SceneObject_CreateEffectModel and Effect_CreateScaledInstance; the create-only body confirms there is no animation-frame update. The body is flagged as damaged decompilation (unaff_ registers), but the create-item/create-effect dispatch and the named GimmickItemEffectStart caller that fix the name are outside the damaged region.

name: maybe_Field_Object_UpdateEffectDirection
summary: Per-frame orientation of an effect part toward a target: computes the unit direction from the object's world position to the tracked node at self+0x28, builds the rotation, calls Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection and counts down self+0x2C, notifying the node when the timer expires.
evidence: The body is a per-frame effect-direction update (Field_Object_GetWorldPosition, Field_SceneNode_GetPosition, Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection, timer at self+0x2C), not the quaternion slerp helper the old name claimed; no caller is known, so the exact trigger stays inferred and the name keeps maybe_ at 0.42.

name: maybe_Actor_UpdateAimPose
summary: Three-axis aim update: converts the node's yaw/pitch/roll fields (+0x304/+0x308/+0x30C) into three quaternion rotations, composes them, plays TurnR/TurnL for the resulting turn and sets the target point/direction on the tracked effect part.
evidence: Re-read next to its named sibling Actor_UpdateTurnAnimation: the body is the three-angle composition with the same s_TurnR/s_TurnL strings and the named Gfx_EffectPart_SetTargetPoint/SetDirection tail, but no IK solve exists anywhere, so 'IK' was dropped. The only caller is the unnamed action-destructor family (0x003E0F3C), so the name stays maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Casino_RollJackpotChanceForCoins
summary: Rolls the casino jackpot probability for a machine slot and the number of coins bet, refreshing the jackpot counters first when the jackpot clock has expired; returns the roll result (0 = no jackpot).
evidence: The named caller Ui_JackpotScreen_StartPayout (0x002C6FE4) passes the slot byte (self+4) and the summed coin count and tests the result against 0, while the body calls the named Casino_IsJackpotClockExpired / Casino_RefreshJackpotCounters and the game RNG (0x0051B1FC); probability-for-coins is the only reading that fits both sides.

name: Ui_TextBuilder_InitLayout
signature: void Ui_TextBuilder_InitLayout(TextBuilder* self, u32 textObj, const u32* styleMask)
summary: Initialises a text builder from a text object: resolves the font metrics and layout box, clamps the origin, selects the active part styles from a bit mask (or from the metrics for multi-style fonts) and computes the per-part baseline/height entries (up to four 0x18-byte descriptors at +0x30).
evidence: The named caller Ui_ListWindow_SelectEntry (0x006258B0) invokes it for multi-line rows after the row lookup and count, and the body calls the named Ui_TextBuilder_SetNumericValues plus the text/layout helpers; initialising the row's text layout is the only reading that fits both sides.

name: maybe_FieldParty_Talk_UpdateMember
summary: Advances the talk-state step of a field party group: resolves the current speaker's character/monster record and actor entry, and when the group reports the animation done it clears the group action state, resets the record and syncs the linked actor states; returns non-zero while the step is still running.
evidence: The named caller FieldParty_Talk_Update (0x0059E134) uses the return value as a state selector (0x39C vs 0x34B) inside its talk loop, and the body calls Field_FindActorEntryByModel/Field_ActorEntry_Copy and iterates group members through the own vtable +0x10C. The exact per-member meaning is not visible, so it keeps maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Effect_MeshEmitter_SetupB
summary: Mesh-emitter setup variant B: stores the emitter record fields, sets the effect node name to the fixed string "Open" at +0x320, applies the placement position/rotation, adds a sprite child with a colour descriptor, registers an fCol animator and creates the mesh from def->+0x42 and variant byte f_11.
evidence: Re-checked against its spawner: maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectMeshEmitterB (0x0034D0B8) allocates the emitter and calls this with the on-stack definition, and the fixed string 0x6E65704F = "Open" is confirmed in the body. 'MeshEmitter' is still inferred from the sibling family rather than a named constructor, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Effect_MeshEmitter_SetupC
summary: Mesh-emitter setup variant C: same sprite child + fCol animator + mesh creation as 0x0040FBB8 but stores the fixed string "Off" at +0x320, sets the variant flag f_318 = 1, takes the mesh id from def->f_F and writes it to +0x312 instead of +0x2C8.
evidence: Re-checked against its spawner: maybe_Field_SceneSpawnBlock_EffectMeshEmitterC (0x0034D454) allocates the emitter and calls this with the on-stack definition, and the fixed string 0x0066664F = "Off" is the counterpart of "Open" in 0x0040FBB8. The class prefix is still a family inference, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Battle_Monster_GetAttackPowerB
summary: Alternate attack-family stat computation for the monster battle UI: performs four record lookups, picks the B constant block (g_00497510 vs g_0049750C) when record->f_665 is clear, and applies the same scaled f_738+f_EB8+f_AF8 formula as 0x00496B50.
evidence: The named caller Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch (0x004920A0) uses it for row kind 8 (the targeted variant) while 0x00496B50 serves kind 10, and Battle_Monster_CalcBarSpan also calls it; that fixes it as the B variant of the same displayed-stat computation, but which stat label it feeds is still not proven, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromDescSmall
summary: Descriptor-driven billboard initialiser: selects the sprite mode from desc byte 0x3E (modes 3/4 also build the quad child), applies the smaller scale/alpha constant set chosen by f_2C9 and creates the mesh.
evidence: Its only caller is still the low-confidence type-C spawner maybe_Field_SceneObject_SpawnByTypeC (0x0035A1D0), which also calls 0x00471ABC; the two differ only in f_2C9 and the scale/length constants, so 'Small' records the measured constant set rather than a verified size class - kept maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromDescLarge
summary: Same descriptor-driven billboard initialiser as 0x004718A4 with f_2C9 = 1 and the larger scale/length constants (3.75/1.5/4.5 instead of 2.5/0.75/4.0).
evidence: Same single low-confidence caller (0x0035A1D0) as its sibling, and the only difference from 0x004718A4 is the f_2C9 flag plus three float constants; 'Large' is the measured constant set, not a proven size class - kept maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Field_PlaceModelAroundActor
signature: void Field_PlaceModelAroundActor(ModelOwner* owner, float* outPos, float* outDir)
summary: Computes a position/direction around an actor, either from its rotation or from a random angle drawn from the game RNG, so a model can be placed relative to it; also ray-checks the resulting spot against the scene.
evidence: The named caller Field_ModelSlotEmitter_SpawnOne (0x004B2FEC) passes the owner and two output vectors and aborts the spawn when the call returns 0, i.e. it is exactly the placement helper for a slot emitter; the body reads the owner transform and otherwise draws a random angle with the game RNG.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_LayoutPartsFromAnchor
summary: Places the actor's parts starting from an anchor: hides the anchor panel through the UI-core vtable +0x28, stores half the anchor distance in f_20 and lays the parts out from the anchor before playing the SE.
evidence: The Ui_GetCore vtable +0x28 (hide) call and the f_20 = f_14>>1 store still support the anchor reading, but no caller or vtable slot names the anchor object, so it stays maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Gfx_UpdateActorsInViewCone
signature: void Gfx_UpdateActorsInViewCone(void* arg1, const float* position, const float* direction)
summary: Walks the field actor list (list id 4) and, for actors of class 0x7C3684 that pass the state checks, measures the distance and the angle between the given direction and the offset; every actor inside the radius and cone receives a vtable+0x38(0x1B, 0) update call.
evidence: The named caller Ui_SpriteMarker_SetTargetFromActor (0x004772C0) passes the marker's position and direction, and the body performs exactly the list walk + vertical/horizontal/angle cone test (same 0x7A6408 angle scale and +0x38 slot as the camera variant) before notifying each matching actor; the earlier objection was about a missing billboard basis, which the name does not claim.

name: maybe_Actor_UpdateDirectionBlend
summary: Per-frame movement integrator for the scripted action ids 0x253..0x25B: blends the actor's direction vector toward the stored target, renormalises it and adds the per-frame motion scaled by an easing factor chosen by actor[0x105], then advances the motion counter and hands the transform to Gfx_Node_UpdateChildren.
evidence: The named callees Os_GetGameWork, std_Powf and Gfx_Node_UpdateChildren confirm a movement/transform integrator rather than a pure facing blend, and the three easing curves plus the counter at actor[0x107] are visible; no caller and no named action ids tie it to a specific move, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Battle_Monster_GetAttackPower
summary: Attack-family stat computation for the monster battle UI: scales the enemy record value f_4 by the base constant block, adds the unsigned f_73C component and recomputes it through 0x00487FC0, then marks the row layout dirty.
evidence: The named caller Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch (0x004920A0) uses it for row kind 10 and its sibling 0x004973E8 for kind 8; that fixes it as the A variant of the same displayed stat, but the body alone (f_73C/f_AF8 scaled values) does not prove the label is attack power, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_MoveAttachmentTowardTarget
summary: Moves the attachment of the referenced actor toward its target: clears the attachment, computes and normalises the direction to the target fields, applies the step (length * factor into f_234) and plays the SE.
evidence: The named callee Field_Actor_UpdateAttachment and the position subtraction/normalisation are clear, but the f_234 = length * factor store is still an unexplained scale and no caller or vtable slot names the gimmick, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Field_Scene_TestPointInBoxSet
summary: Tests a world point against the scene's 0x60-byte oriented-box set (copied from scene+0x38C): it converts each box to its local frame through Math_BuildQuaternionFromEuler and stops at the first box that contains the point. The decompiled signature is void, so the boolean result visible at each hit path was probably dropped.
evidence: Re-read the body: the old 'AbortIfPointInBoxSet' was wrong because a normal function cannot abort its caller - every hit path simply returns, which is the classic Ghidra-dropped return value (damaged signature), and the caller Event_Rura_Start (0x004F18A4) ignores the result. The box-set test itself is certain, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Ui_Layout_BuildQuadTransforms
signature: void maybe_Ui_Layout_BuildQuadTransforms(LayoutSet* self, u32 dst, u32 count, LayoutEntry* entries, float scale)
summary: Turns the layout element's 0x14-byte sprite records into per-quad vertex coordinates (8 floats each), handling rotation through std_FastSinCos, the arbitrary-quad UV path and the 'use element transform' entry kinds, and caches the result (entry count at +100, built flag bit 3 of f_7C, flags f_65/f_66).
evidence: Both callers are now named UI-layout text writers (Ui_LayoutText_AppendGlyphPositions 0x0053C384 and Ui_LayoutText_AppendGlyphTexCoords 0x0053A824), and the callee Ui_LayoutElement_BuildTransform plus std_FastSinCos place it in the layout library; the old 'Gfx_Sprite' prefix named the wrong subsystem, but the owning class is still not fully proven, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Menu_UpdateModelFadeIn
summary: Drives the fade-in of the displayed party's 3D models: waits until all four sub-groups report ready, advances the fade step counter up to 3, and averages the per-actor fade values through the actor virtual +0x24/+0x18 calls.
evidence: The only named caller is maybe_Battle_UpdateUnitDisplay (0x002D9E00), not a camp-menu function, so the old 'Camp' qualifier was unproven and has been dropped; the fade-step and per-actor averaging are unchanged, and the display context is still ambiguous (battle display vs menu), so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_UpdateSlotTransforms
signature: void maybe_Ui_Part_UpdateSlotTransforms(void* part, u32 frame, u32* timer)
summary: Per-frame transform update for an effect part: rebuilds up to four slot rotations from the three angle fields with the shared trig helpers, applies the stored transform blocks and clamps the part bounding box.
evidence: The trig/matrix sequence and the four 0x20-stride slots are clear, and the callers include the named Math_ComputeRotatedAabb and Sound_Emitter_SetPositionAndDirection, but the owning class is still ambiguous (also called from the jockey panel release), so the Ui_Part prefix stays maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Ui_System_InitSlotPool
summary: One-shot initialisation of the UI system: seeds the twelve shared constants at +0x6E4..+0x710, allocates the 0x300-byte block, default-constructs its 64 entries of 0xC bytes and clears the pool count at +0x12AC.
evidence: The named caller Ui_Core_Init (0x00625C44) invokes it right after allocating the 0x12B0-byte UI system object, and the body's lazy-init flag at +8, Mem_AllocAligned(0x300, ..., 4) and std_ConstructArray(..., 0xC, 0x40) + count reset match the slot-pool construction; the caller passes no explicit argument because the register forwarding was dropped by Ghidra (FACTS: dropped registers), not because the parameter is unused.

name: Ui_JackpotScreen_UpdateReelResult
